title: Garlic Beef Skillet
shortDescription: Ground beef, tortillas, and enchilada sauce in one pan for ten
subtitle: Ground beef, tortillas, and enchilada sauce in one pan for ten
description: Ground beef browns with spices and onions, then simmers with torn tortillas and enchilada sauce until bubbly. Top with cheese and bake until melted for a fast Mexican comfort feed.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Beef Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef with onion over medium-high heat 8–10 minutes, breaking into crumbles until browned. Drain excess fat. Stir in garlic, chili powder, and cumin 1 minute. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Layer the skillet
steps.instruction: Add half the torn tortillas, half the enchilada sauce, and half the beef. Repeat layers, ending with sauce on top. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer on stove
steps.instruction: Cover and simmer on low 10 minutes until tortillas soften and absorb sauce. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake with cheese
steps.instruction: Top with cheddar and bake uncovered at 375°F until cheese melts and bubbles at edges, about 15 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Scoop portions with spatula and top with sour cream and cilantro at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Add a can of black beans for stretch and fiber without changing the vibe.
Pickled jalapeños on the side beat cooking spice into the whole batch.
Two skillets bake faster than one deep hotel pan if your oven runs small.
tonightSpread: Skillet scoops with sour cream, cilantro, and shredded lettuce on the side.
Mexican rice in a hotel pan for crew who want a bigger plate.
leftovers: Reheat covered at 350°F with extra sauce splashed on top.
Stuff into burritos with scrambled eggs for breakfast shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Enchilada flavor without rolling dozens of tortillas. One skillet bakes in the oven while you set up the rest of the meal, and it scoops fast when the tones drop.
mealPrepNotes: Use stale tortillas—they absorb sauce better. Brown beef hard for flavor. Assemble in an oven-safe skillet or transfer to hotel pans for baking.
